questions.stemHtml: Image shows normal graph and the patient's graph with FEV1 & FVC. What is the diagnosis?Normal PatientFEV1 = 3.3 FEV1 = 1.0FVC = 4 FVC = 2.0FEV1/FVC = 83% FEV1/FVC = 50%
questions.solutionHtml:
Bronchiectasis

The patient graph shows a reduction in FEV1/FVC which is suggestive of an obstructive lung disease. Among the given options, the likely diagnosis is bronchiectasis.



Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology - 26th edition - page 617, 618.

questions.stem: Components of the limbic system?AmygdalaHypothalamusHippocampusChoose the correct answer:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,2,3
  • This option includes all three components of the limbic system, namely the amygdala, hypothalamus, and hippocampus.
  • This is the correct answer as it includes all the major components of the limbic system involved in emotion, memory, and various physiological processes.

questions.stem: Mechanism of action of poisoning due to canned uncooked meat is?

options.label: C
options.text: Inhibition of of brush border villi

questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibition of NMJ

Eating raw uncooked or canned meat can cause botulism. The spores germinate and the botulinum toxin released inhibits acetylcholine release at NMJ thereby causing flaccid paralysis.



Guyton and Hall, Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page No. 465

questions.stemHtml: A 35 year old female patient had developed vesico-bullous disorder which shows fishnet appearance on IF as shown below on skin biopsy. A diagnosis of pemphigus vulgaris is made. Which among the following describes the disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Autoimmune disorder where antibodies are formed against hemidesmosomes.

options.label: B
options.text: Autoimmune disorder with anti connexon antibodies.

options.label: C
options.text: Disease with poorly formed cell adhesion molecules.

options.label: D
options.text: Autoimmune disorder where antibodies are formed against desmosomes

questions.answerText: Autoimmune disorder where antibodies are formed against desmosomes
questions.solutionHtml:
Autoimmune disorder where antibodies are formed against desmosomes
  • Pemphigus vulgaris is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the presence of antibodies against desmosomes, which are cell adhesion molecules. Desmosomes are responsible for maintaining the integrity and cohesion of epithelial cells. In pemphigus vulgaris, autoantibodies target desmogleins, which are proteins present in desmosomes.
  • The fishnet appearance observed on immunofluorescence (IF) is due to the deposition of antibodies around individual epidermal cells.


Guyton and Hall, Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page No. 54
